desc_src: This scene is the moving conclusion of the story of Tobias, the young man at the right. It addresses the themes of family devotion and trust. Tobias’s father sent him on a long journey to retrieve family money. The angel Raphael appeared as a relative, offering the traveler protection against such things as an attack by a huge fish, whose organs Tobias took on Raphael’s advice. Upon his return home, Tobias discovers his father has gone blind, and Raphael advises him to place the fish’s gallbladder on his father’s eyes to cure him. Following Cubist principles, this painting depicts a table from multiple perspectives, providing different views of various objects simultaneously. Louis Casimir Ladislas Markus was born in Warsaw, Poland, into a Jewish family that had converted to Catholicism. In 1903, he moved to Paris where he met poet Guillaume Apollinaire and artists Georges Braque and Pablo Picasso. He then began experimenting with Cubism. When posed in this powerful and exuberant manner, the image of Hanuman stood at the top of a standard. As the son of the wind god and the most powerful of the primeval forest-dwellers, who are depicted with the head and tail of a monkey and the body of a man, Hanuman as an emblem spelled success in battle.

Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a house and dog. To deposit a coin, the dog is pulled back and the coin placed on a platter in its mouth. Raising the dog's tail releases the action, causing the dog to shoot forward, depositing the coin in the house. Manufactured by the H.L. Judd Company circa 1880. Title: Gem Mechanical Coin Bank
Cast iron bank depicting a cat on top of a hatching egg. Coin slot is on top of the cat's back. When a coin is deposited the hatching chicken's head moves. Title: Tabby Mechanical Coin Bank

Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a cabin with a African American man at the door. To deposit money you must place a coin on the roof and pull the broom handle on the side of the cabin. The man will then flip up and kick the coin into the bank. Manufactured by the J and E Stevens Company circa 1885. Title: Cabin Mechanical Coin Bank

An x-ray far-field interferometer using only phase gratings is based on the phase moiré effect. The mid grating forms Fourier images of the first grating. These images beat with the 3rd grating to produce broad moiré fringes on the detector at the appropriate distance. Phase shifts and de-coherence of the wavefront by the object cause fringe shifts and attenuation of the fringe contrast.

An x-ray far-field interferometer using only phase gratings is based on the phase moire effect. The mid grating forms Fourier images of the first grating. These images beat with the 3rd grating to produce broad moire fringes on the detector at the appropriate distance. Phase shifts and de-coherence of the wavefront by the object cause fringe shifts and attenuation of the fringe contrast.
